title: On Submitting the accounts every March
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：submit　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 submit 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1962 the craftsman ① submitted the accounts every March in silence, and every apprentice in the workshop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the craftsman ② submits the accounts every March twice over without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ submit the accounts every March at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ submitted the accounts every March before — a line in the ledger for August 1956 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Submitting the accounts every March in silence, the craftsman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the tool at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ submit to the decision without a word twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Submit to the decision without a word at once and never mention it again.

By 1969 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the ledger, and a new apprentice from the next workshop ⑧ submits to the decision without a word in silence every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ submitted the accounts every March again when nobody else would.

⑩ To submit the accounts every March, my mother said in 1974, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the workshop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the workshop forgets, somebody submits the accounts every March twice over again and somebody must submit the accounts every March in silence all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 提交（一般过去式 submitted the accounts every March：1962 年匠人头一回这样做，一言不发地）
B. v. 提交（一般现在 submits the accounts every March：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 提交（不定式 to submit the accounts every March：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 提交（过去完成时 had submitted the accounts every March：1956 年八月的工料簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 提交（动名词 submitting the accounts every March 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 屈服（submit to the decision without a word：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去屈服一言不发接受了这个决定）
G. v. 屈服（submit to the decision without a word：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 提交（后段两处：新来的学徒照例 submits to the decision without a word，而母亲又一次 submitted the accounts every March）

answers.why: submit 意为“提交”，1962 年匠人一言不发地提交每年三月呈上那些账目，那是工坊里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 submitted。
submit 意为“提交”，自那以后匠人来回两遍把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 submits。
submit 意为“提交”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯提交每年三月呈上那些账目”，此处为不定式 to submit the accounts every March。
submit 意为“提交”，工料簿里 八月 那行字说明早在 1969 年之前就有人提交过，故用过去完成时 had submitted。
submit 意为“提交”，匠人说“提交每年三月呈上那些账目这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 submitting the accounts every March 作主语。
submit 意为“屈服”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去屈服一言不发接受了这个决定”，should ever 之后用原形 submit to the decision without a word。
submit 意为“屈服”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻屈服一言不发接受了这个决定（submit to the decision without a word at once），以后再也不要提起。
submit 意为“提交”，新来的学徒每个年头都照例屈服一言不发接受了这个决定，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 submits。
submit 意为“提交”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次一言不发地提交每年三月呈上那些账目，用一般过去式 submitted 叙述。
submit 意为“提交”，结尾那句是母亲 1974 年的话：要提交每年三月呈上那些账目，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和工坊记住的那一件。

多年以后，匠人仍来回两遍做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（submits the accounts every March）

老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻屈服一言不发接受了这个决定，以后再也不要提起。（submit to the decision without a word，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 submit 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1962 the craftsman submitted the accounts every March in silence, and nobody in the workshop forgot it.
Even now the craftsman submits the accounts every March twice over whenever the workshop asks.
Submitting the accounts every March in silence, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever submit to the decision without a word twice over, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new apprentice from the next workshop submits to the decision without a word in silence every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother submitted the accounts every March again, and the workshop remembered that half.
